subject.title: [Feature]: Add $EDITOR compose mode in TUI (external editor handoff) for multiline prompts

question: Should OpenClaw add a core TUI external-editor compose handoff now, and what trigger plus local editor/temp-file safety contract should it use?
rationale: The missing capability is clear, but launching `$VISUAL` or `$EDITOR` and writing prompt drafts to disk crosses local process execution and sensitive-content boundaries that automation should not choose alone.

options.title: Approve Guarded Core Flow
options.body: Implement the handoff in core TUI with an approved key or slash trigger, argv-safe editor handling, restrictive temp files, cleanup, no auto-submit, visible errors, tests, and docs.

options.title: Hold For UX And Safety Contract
options.body: Keep the issue open until maintainers choose the permanent trigger and document the local editor/tempfile rules.

options.title: Decline Local Editor Handoff
options.body: Prefer inline multiline editing, composer expansion, or another non-process-launch path and close or narrow this request by maintainer decision.

recommendation.title: Approve Guarded Core Flow
recommendation.body: Implement the handoff in core TUI with an approved key or slash trigger, argv-safe editor handling, restrictive temp files, cleanup, no auto-submit, visible errors, tests, and docs.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest TUI ownership trail and already framed the issue's remaining product and security decision in prior review context.
